notes:
1. Meaning of Election

  • An election is the process through which citizens choose representatives to govern on their behalf.
  • In a representative democracy, citizens elect representatives instead of directly participating in every governmental decision.

Elections create the constitutional link between:

  • People.
  • Legislature.
  • Government.

2. Institutions Chosen through Elections

Important elected institutions include:

  • Lok Sabha.
  • State Legislative Assemblies.
  • Local Bodies.
  • Rajya Sabha and Legislative Councils through indirect electoral methods.

3. Importance of Elections

Elections:

  • Give legitimacy to Government.
  • Ensure political accountability.
  • Enable peaceful transfer of power.
  • Represent public opinion.
  • Encourage political participation.
  • Protect representative democracy.
  • Allow voters to choose between candidates and parties.

4. Consent of the People

A democratically elected Government derives political authority from:

  • Consent of the people.

Elections periodically allow voters to:

  • Approve representatives.
  • Reject representatives.
  • Change ruling parties.

5. Free and Fair Elections

Free and fair elections require voters to exercise choice without:

  • Fear.
  • Coercion.
  • Bribery.
  • Intimidation.
  • Administrative interference.
  • Electoral discrimination.
📌 Must-Memorise

Free and Fair Elections → Essential to Democratic Legitimacy

6. Equal Electoral Opportunity

The election process should provide:

  • Legal equality.
  • Fair opportunity.
  • Impartial administration

for candidates and political parties within the framework of election law.

7. Part XV

The principal constitutional provisions relating to elections are contained in:

  • Part XV.
  • Articles 324–329.
📌 Must-Memorise

Elections → Part XV → Articles 324–329

8. Article 324

Article 324 vests:

  • Superintendence.
  • Direction.
  • Control

of specified elections in:

  • Election Commission of India.
📌 Must-Memorise

Article 324 → Election Commission of India

9. Elections Conducted by ECI

The Election Commission conducts elections to:

  • Lok Sabha.
  • Rajya Sabha.
  • State Legislative Assemblies.
  • State Legislative Councils.
  • President.
  • Vice-President.

10. Elections Not Conducted by ECI

The Election Commission of India does not conduct elections to:

  • Panchayats.
  • Municipalities.

These are conducted by:

  • State Election Commission.

11. Article 243K

Article 243K deals with:

  • State Election Commission for Panchayat elections.

12. Article 243ZA

Article 243ZA deals with:

  • Elections to Municipalities through State Election Commission.
📌 Must-Memorise

243K → Panchayats 243ZA → Municipalities

13. Article 325

Article 325 provides for:

  • One General Electoral Roll for every territorial constituency.
📌 Must-Memorise

Article 325 → One General Electoral Roll

14. No Electoral-Roll Discrimination

No person may be excluded from an electoral roll solely on grounds of:

  • Religion.
  • Race.
  • Caste.
  • Sex.

15. Separate Communal Electorates

Article 325 rejects the system of:

  • Separate communal electorates.
  • The electoral roll is common for eligible citizens.

16. Article 326

Article 326 provides that elections to:

  • Lok Sabha.
  • State Legislative Assemblies

shall be based on:

  • Universal Adult Suffrage.
📌 Must-Memorise

Article 326 → Universal Adult Suffrage

17. Meaning of Universal Adult Suffrage

Universal Adult Suffrage means every eligible adult citizen may vote without discrimination based on:

  • Religion.
  • Race.
  • Caste.
  • Sex.
  • Wealth.
  • Education.
  • Social status.

18. Present Voting Age

The voting age is:

  • 18 years.

19. Original Voting Age

The original constitutional voting age was:

  • 21 years.

20. Sixty-First Constitutional Amendment

The 61st Constitutional Amendment Act, 1988 reduced voting age:

  • From 21 years.
  • To 18 years.
📌 Must-Memorise

61st Amendment → 1988 → Voting Age 21 → 18

21. Significance of Lower Voting Age

The reduction:

  • Expanded the electorate.
  • Increased youth participation.
  • Strengthened Universal Adult Suffrage.

22. Article 327

Article 327 empowers Parliament to legislate regarding elections to:

  • Parliament.
  • State Legislatures.
📌 Must-Memorise

Article 327 → Parliament's Election-Law Power

23. Article 328

Article 328 empowers a State Legislature to legislate regarding elections to:

  • That State Legislature

subject to:

  • Constitution.
  • Parliamentary law.

24. Article 329

Article 329 limits judicial interference during an ongoing election process.

📌 Must-Memorise

Article 329 → Bar on Court Interference during Election Process

25. Election Petition

Validity of an election is ordinarily challenged through:

  • Election Petition.
  • The challenge is made after completion of election according to applicable law.

26. Purpose of Article 329

The objective is to prevent:

  • Repeated judicial interruptions.
  • Disruption of an ongoing election process.

27. Article 71

Article 71 provides that disputes relating to elections of:

  • President.
  • Vice-President

are decided by:

  • Supreme Court.
📌 Must-Memorise

Article 71 → President and Vice-President Election Disputes → Supreme Court

28. Representation of the People Act, 1950

The Representation of the People Act, 1950 mainly deals with:

  • Allocation of seats.
  • Electoral-roll framework.
  • Voter registration.
  • Electoral-roll preparation.
  • Delimitation-related electoral structure.
📌 Must-Memorise

RPA 1950 → Seats + Electoral Rolls + Voter Registration

29. Representation of the People Act, 1951

The Representation of the People Act, 1951 mainly deals with:

  • Conduct of elections.
  • Qualifications.
  • Disqualifications.
  • Corrupt practices.
  • Election offences.
  • Election disputes.
  • Political-party registration.
📌 Must-Memorise

RPA 1951 → Conduct + Disqualification + Corrupt Practices + Election Petitions

30. Direct Election

In direct elections:

  • Voters directly elect representatives.

Examples include:

  • Lok Sabha.
  • Legislative Assemblies.
  • Panchayats.
  • Municipalities.

31. Indirect Election

In indirect elections, representatives or office-holders are chosen by:

  • Electoral College.
  • Elected representatives.
  • Specified electoral bodies.

32. Examples of Indirect Elections

The attachment lists:

  • President.
  • Vice-President.
  • Rajya Sabha.
  • Legislative Councils.

33. First-Past-the-Post System

India generally uses:

  • First-Past-the-Post system

for:

  • Lok Sabha elections.
  • State Legislative Assembly elections.
📌 Must-Memorise

Lok Sabha + Assembly → FPTP

34. FPTP Rule

Under FPTP:

  • Candidate securing the highest number of valid votes wins.
  • Absolute majority of total votes is not required.
⚠️ TNPSC Trap

FPTP Winner → Highest Votes Not Necessarily → More than 50%

35. Proportional Representation

Proportional Representation is used in specified indirect elections.

The attachment associates PR by Single Transferable Vote with elections such as:

  • President.
  • Vice-President.
  • Rajya Sabha.
  • Certain Legislative Council members.

36. Single Transferable Vote

Under STV:

  • Preferences are transferred according to prescribed electoral rules.
  • It is used in specified constitutional indirect elections.

37. Secret Ballot

Secret Ballot protects:

  • Privacy of voter's choice.
  • Electoral freedom.
  • Independence from pressure.

38. Purpose of Secret Ballot

It protects voters against:

  • Retaliation.
  • Coercion.
  • Social pressure.
  • Political intimidation.

39. Electoral Constituency

A constituency is:

  • A defined territorial area from which a representative is elected.

40. Territorial Constituencies

Lok Sabha and Assembly elections are organised through:

  • Territorial constituencies.
  • Each constituency ordinarily elects one representative under the applicable system.

41. Electoral Roll

An electoral roll is:

  • Official list of eligible voters in a constituency.

42. Importance of Electoral Roll

A person must ordinarily have:

  • Name entered in relevant electoral roll

to vote in the constituency.

43. Voter Registration Eligibility

The attachment identifies conditions such as:

  • Indian citizenship.
  • Age of at least 18.
  • Ordinary residence in relevant constituency.
  • No legal disqualification.

44. Preparation of Electoral Rolls

Under ECI supervision, the process includes:

  • New registrations.
  • Corrections.
  • Deletion of ineligible names.
  • Inclusion of eligible citizens.
  • Periodic revision.

45. Election Commission of India

ECI is:

  • Independent constitutional authority.
  • Responsible for conducting free and fair elections within its constitutional jurisdiction.

46. Original Composition of ECI

Originally, Election Commission consisted of:

  • Chief Election Commissioner only.

47. Present Composition in the Attachment

The attachment records Election Commission as a multi-member body consisting of:

  • Chief Election Commissioner.
  • Two Election Commissioners.
📌 Must-Memorise

ECI → CEC + 2 Election Commissioners in Source

48. Number of Election Commissioners

  • President may determine the number of Election Commissioners according to applicable constitutional and legal framework.

49. Appointment of CEC

Chief Election Commissioner is appointed by:

  • President of India

in accordance with the law in force.

50. Appointment of Election Commissioners

Other Election Commissioners are also appointed by:

  • President of India

according to applicable law.

51. Tenure

The source records tenure as:

  • Six years.
  • Or until 65 years of age.
  • Whichever is earlier.
📌 Must-Memorise

CEC/EC → 6 Years or 65 Years, Whichever Earlier

52. Resignation

Chief Election Commissioner and Election Commissioners may resign to:

  • President.

53. Removal of Chief Election Commissioner

CEC may be removed:

  • In same manner.
  • On same grounds

as:

  • Judge of Supreme Court.
📌 Must-Memorise

CEC Removal → Same as Supreme Court Judge

54. Removal of Other Election Commissioners

Other Election Commissioners cannot be removed except on:

  • Recommendation of Chief Election Commissioner.
⚠️ TNPSC Favourite

CEC → Stronger Removal Protection EC → Removal on CEC Recommendation

55. Independence of ECI

Important safeguards include:

  • Constitutional status.
  • Security of tenure.
  • Protected removal process.
  • Independent decision-making.
  • Protection from executive interference.
  • Specified financial safeguards provided by law.

56. Types of ECI Powers

The source classifies ECI powers as:

  • Administrative.
  • Advisory.
  • Quasi-judicial.
  • Supervisory.

57. Election Scheduling

ECI:

  • Announces election schedules.
  • Coordinates stages of election.
  • Supervises implementation of election timetable.

58. Poll Supervision

ECI supervises:

  • Polling.
  • Election machinery.
  • Counting.
  • Declaration of results.

59. Political-Party Recognition

ECI recognises political parties as:

  • National Parties.
  • State Parties

according to applicable criteria under election law and symbols framework.

60. Election Symbols

ECI:

  • Allots election symbols.
  • Resolves symbol disputes.
  • Regulates reserved and free symbols.

61. Reserved Symbols

Reserved Symbols are associated with:

  • Recognised National Parties.
  • Recognised State Parties.

62. Free Symbols

Free Symbols may be allotted to:

  • Independent candidates.
  • Registered unrecognised political parties

subject to applicable rules.

63. Importance of Election Symbols

Symbols help voters:

  • Identify candidates.
  • Identify parties.
  • Participate effectively in a diverse electorate.

64. Model Code of Conduct

The Model Code of Conduct is a set of guidelines issued and enforced by:

  • Election Commission of India.
📌 Must-Memorise

MCC → Election Commission Guidelines

65. When MCC Begins

The MCC comes into force:

  • Immediately after Election Commission announces election schedule.

66. Duration of MCC

It continues until:

  • Completion of election process.

67. Purpose of MCC

It seeks to:

  • Maintain level playing field.
  • Prevent misuse of official machinery.
  • Promote fair campaigning.
  • Prevent communal and inflammatory appeals.
  • Support free and fair elections.

68. Government Machinery under MCC

Government machinery should not be used for:

  • Electoral campaigning.
  • Unfair partisan advantage.

69. Public Funds under MCC

Public funds should not be misused for:

  • Electoral benefit.
  • Partisan publicity.

70. New Schemes during MCC

Ministers should avoid announcing:

  • New schemes.
  • New projects

that may influence voters during election period.

71. Religious Places

Religious places should not be used for:

  • Election propaganda.

72. Legal Nature of MCC

  • MCC is not itself a law enacted by Parliament.
  • It operates as a code of political conduct under ECI supervision.
  • Existing statutory provisions may separately apply to prohibited conduct.
⚠️ TNPSC Trap

MCC → Not a Parliamentary Statute

73. Election Expenditure Monitoring

ECI monitors:

  • Candidate expenditure.
  • Campaign expenses.
  • Compliance with prescribed expenditure limits.

74. Election Observers

The source lists:

  • General Observers.
  • Expenditure Observers.
  • Police Observers.

75. Purpose of Observers

Observers help ensure:

  • Fairness.
  • Transparency.
  • Lawful administration.
  • Expenditure compliance.
  • Security supervision.

76. Advisory Role of ECI

ECI advises:

  • President on specified MP disqualification questions.
  • Governor on specified State-legislator disqualification questions.

77. Quasi-Judicial Role

ECI performs quasi-judicial functions in matters such as:

  • Political-party recognition.
  • Election-symbol disputes.

78. Election Commission vs State Election Commission

ECI:

  • Article 324.
  • Parliament and State Legislature elections.
  • President and Vice-President elections.

State Election Commission:

  • Articles 243K and 243ZA.
  • Panchayat and Municipal elections.

79. Delimitation

Delimitation means:

  • Determining.
  • Redrawing

territorial boundaries of electoral constituencies.

80. Purpose of Delimitation

It seeks to:

  • Improve equality of representation.
  • Balance constituency populations.
  • Prevent malapportionment.
  • Reflect demographic changes.

81. Delimitation Commission

Delimitation is carried out by:

  • Delimitation Commission

constituted under the relevant:

  • Delimitation Act.

82. Independence of Delimitation Commission

The Commission functions independently while carrying out:

  • Boundary readjustment.
  • Constituency delimitation.

83. Reservation of Constituencies

The Delimitation Commission also deals with reserved constituencies for:

  • Scheduled Castes.
  • Scheduled Tribes

according to constitutional and population criteria.

84. Delimitation Freeze

The source states that seat readjustment is constitutionally frozen until readjustment based on:

  • First Census conducted after 2026

takes effect according to constitutional provisions.

📌 Must-Memorise

Seat Readjustment → Linked to First Census after 2026 in Source

85. Delimitation vs Electoral Roll

Delimitation:

  • Draws constituency boundaries.
  • Deals with territorial representation.

Electoral Roll:

  • Lists eligible voters.
  • Determines who may vote.

86. Election Notification

The formal electoral process begins with:

  • Election Notification.

87. Election Notification Contents

It specifies dates relating to:

  • Nominations.
  • Polling.
  • Counting.
  • Election schedule.

88. Nomination Paper

A person wishing to contest must file:

  • Nomination Paper

before:

  • Returning Officer

within prescribed time.

89. Security Deposit

A candidate must deposit:

  • Prescribed security amount

when filing nomination.

The deposit may be forfeited according to election law.

90. Scrutiny of Nominations

Returning Officer examines:

  • Candidate qualifications.
  • Disqualifications.
  • Compliance with nomination requirements.

91. Rejection of Nomination

A nomination may be rejected where:

  • Candidate lacks qualification.
  • Candidate is disqualified.
  • Statutory requirements are not satisfied.

92. Withdrawal of Candidature

After scrutiny:

  • Candidate may withdraw within prescribed period.
  • Final list of contesting candidates is then published.

93. Election Campaign

Campaigning may involve:

  • Public meetings.
  • Door-to-door canvassing.
  • Print media.
  • Electronic media.
  • Social media.
  • Election manifestos.

94. Campaign Regulation

Campaigns must comply with:

  • Election laws.
  • Model Code of Conduct.
  • Expenditure limits.

95. Polling Station

Polling takes place at:

  • Polling Stations

established for voters in constituencies.

96. One Voter, One Vote

Every eligible voter appearing on the electoral roll may cast:

  • One vote

in the applicable election.

97. Electronic Voting Machine

EVM is an electronic device used to:

  • Record votes.

98. Main EVM Components

The source identifies:

  • Ballot Unit.
  • Control Unit.
  • VVPAT where used.

99. Advantages of EVM

The attachment identifies:

  • Faster polling.
  • Faster counting.
  • Reduced invalid votes.
  • Administrative efficiency.
  • Lower paper use.

100. VVPAT

VVPAT stands for:

  • Voter Verifiable Paper Audit Trail.
📌 Must-Memorise

VVPAT → Voter Verifiable Paper Audit Trail

101. Purpose of VVPAT

VVPAT allows voters to verify:

  • Vote was recorded for intended candidate.

102. VVPAT Slip

After a vote:

  • Candidate name and symbol appear briefly on a paper slip.
  • Slip is stored securely inside the machine.
  • Voter does not take the slip away.

103. Importance of VVPAT

VVPAT supports:

  • Transparency.
  • Audit trail.
  • Voter confidence.
  • Verification according to applicable procedures.

104. Counting of Votes

After polling:

  • EVMs are securely transported.
  • Counting occurs at designated centres.
  • Returning Officer supervises counting.

105. Persons Present during Counting

The source identifies:

  • Candidates.
  • Election agents.
  • Observers.

106. Declaration of Results

Under FPTP:

  • Candidate securing highest number of valid votes is declared elected.
  • Returning Officer declares result.

107. Electoral Process Sequence

The source gives the sequence:

  • Electoral Roll.
  • Delimitation when applicable.
  • Election Notification.
  • Nominations.
  • Scrutiny.
  • Withdrawal.
  • Campaign.
  • Polling.
  • Counting.
  • Declaration of Results.
  • Election Petition, where required.

108. Meaning of Electoral Reforms

Electoral reforms are measures introduced to improve:

  • Fairness.
  • Transparency.
  • Efficiency.
  • Accountability.
  • Public confidence.

109. Major Electoral Reforms in the Source

The attachment includes:

  • Voting age reduced to 18.
  • EVMs.
  • VVPAT.
  • Candidate disclosure.
  • NOTA.
  • Expenditure monitoring.
  • Photo Electoral Rolls.
  • EPIC.
  • Greater use of technology.

110. EPIC

EPIC stands for:

  • Elector Photo Identity Card.

111. Purpose of EPIC

EPIC helps:

  • Verify voter identity.
  • Prevent impersonation.
  • Improve transparency.
  • Support genuine voting.

112. NOTA

NOTA stands for:

  • None of the Above.
📌 Must-Memorise

NOTA → None of the Above

113. Introduction of NOTA

NOTA was introduced following:

  • People's Union for Civil Liberties v. Union of India, 2013.
📌 Must-Memorise

PUCL, 2013 → NOTA

114. Purpose of NOTA

NOTA allows a voter to:

  • Reject all contesting candidates.
  • Still participate in voting.
  • Preserve secrecy of choice.

115. Effect of NOTA

According to the attachment:

  • Candidate securing highest valid votes is elected even if NOTA obtains more votes than an individual candidate.
⚠️ TNPSC Trap

NOTA Highest → Does Not Automatically Trigger Re-Election under Source Framework

116. Candidate Disclosure

Candidates are required to disclose information regarding:

  • Criminal cases.
  • Assets.
  • Liabilities.
  • Educational qualifications.

117. Purpose of Candidate Disclosure

It helps voters:

  • Make informed choices.
  • Assess candidate background.
  • Improve electoral transparency.

118. Criminalisation of Politics

The source identifies as a major electoral challenge:

  • Participation of candidates with serious criminal cases.
  • Need for disclosure and reform.

119. Paid News

Paid News refers to:

  • News or media content published for payment without proper disclosure as paid publicity.

120. Problems Caused by Paid News

Paid News undermines:

  • Electoral fairness.
  • Transparency.
  • Informed voting.

121. Other Electoral Challenges

The source identifies:

  • Money power.
  • Criminalisation.
  • Paid news.
  • Misuse of Government machinery.
  • Electoral misinformation.
  • Voter inducement.
  • Low political awareness.
  • Hate speech.
  • Weak internal party democracy.

122. Article 84

Article 84 deals with:

  • Qualifications for Parliament.

123. Parliamentary Qualifications

A person must:

  • Be citizen of India.
  • Make prescribed oath or affirmation.
  • Possess statutory qualifications.
  • Meet minimum age requirement.

124. Lok Sabha Minimum Age

Minimum age:

  • 25 years.

125. Rajya Sabha Minimum Age

Minimum age:

  • 30 years.
📌 Must-Memorise

Lok Sabha → 25 Rajya Sabha → 30

126. Article 173

Article 173 deals with:

  • Qualifications for State Legislature.

127. Legislative Assembly Minimum Age

Minimum age:

  • 25 years.

128. Legislative Council Minimum Age

Minimum age:

  • 30 years.
📌 Must-Memorise

Assembly → 25 Council → 30

129. Article 102

Article 102 deals with:

  • Disqualifications for Parliament.

130. Article 191

Article 191 deals with:

  • Disqualifications for State Legislature.

131. Office of Profit

A legislator may be disqualified for holding:

  • Office of Profit under Government

unless exempted by law.

132. Purpose of Office-of-Profit Rule

The rule seeks to:

  • Preserve legislative independence.
  • Prevent undue executive influence.
  • Avoid conflict of interest.

133. Unsound Mind

Disqualification applies where:

  • Person is of unsound mind.
  • Competent Court has formally declared it.

134. Undischarged Insolvent

A person who is:

  • Legally insolvent.
  • Not yet discharged

may be disqualified.

135. Citizenship Disqualification

Disqualification may arise where a person:

  • Is not an Indian citizen.
  • Voluntarily acquires foreign citizenship.
  • Acknowledges allegiance to foreign State.

136. Statutory Disqualifications

Parliament may prescribe additional grounds through:

  • Representation of the People Act, 1951.

137. Corrupt Practices

The source lists examples including:

  • Bribery.
  • Undue influence.
  • Prohibited electoral appeals.
  • Other statutory electoral malpractices.

138. Criminal Conviction

Certain convictions may result in disqualification under:

  • Representation of the People Act, 1951.

139. Tenth Schedule

The Tenth Schedule contains:

  • Anti-Defection Law.

140. Defection Grounds

A legislator may be disqualified for:

  • Voluntarily giving up party membership.
  • Voting or abstaining contrary to party direction under conditions specified by Tenth Schedule.

141. Authority under Anti-Defection Law

The source identifies:

  • Lok Sabha/Assembly → Speaker.
  • Rajya Sabha/Legislative Council → Chairman.

142. Judicial Review of Defection Decisions

Decisions under Tenth Schedule are subject to:

  • Judicial Review

according to Supreme Court jurisprudence.

143. MP Disqualification Decision

For specified constitutional disqualification questions concerning MPs:

  • President decides.

President acts according to opinion of:

  • Election Commission of India.

144. State Legislator Disqualification Decision

For specified constitutional disqualification questions concerning State legislators:

  • Governor decides.

Governor acts according to opinion of:

  • Election Commission of India.

145. Fifty-Second Constitutional Amendment, 1985

The 52nd Amendment:

  • Inserted Tenth Schedule.
  • Introduced Anti-Defection Law.
📌 Must-Memorise

52nd Amendment → Anti-Defection

  • Scheduled Castes.
  • Scheduled Tribes

in:

  • Lok Sabha.

  • Liabilities.
  • Educational qualifications.

159. Voters' Right to Know

The ADR judgment strengthened:

  • Voters' Right to Know.
  • Informed electoral participation.
  • Candidate transparency.

160. PUCL v. Union of India, 2003

The Supreme Court recognised:

Secrecy of voting as an important aspect of:

  • Free and Fair Elections.
📌 Must-Memorise

PUCL 2003 → Secrecy of Voting

161. PUCL v. Union of India, 2013

The Supreme Court directed introduction of:

  • NOTA.

162. Importance of NOTA Judgment

What is an election? → Process by which citizens choose representatives.

Why are elections important? → Legitimacy, accountability, peaceful transfer of power, participation and representation.

Which Part of Constitution deals principally with elections? → Part XV.

What is its Article range? → Articles 324–329.

Which Article establishes constitutional authority of ECI? → Article 324.

What three expressions are used in Article 324? → Superintendence, Direction and Control.

Which elections does ECI conduct according to the attachment? → Parliament, State Legislatures, President and Vice-President.

Does ECI conduct Panchayat elections? → No.

Which body does? → State Election Commission.

Which Article deals with Panchayat elections? → Article 243K.

Which Article deals with Municipal elections? → Article 243ZA.

Which Article provides One General Electoral Roll? → Article 325.

On what grounds can a person not be excluded solely from an electoral roll? → Religion, Race, Caste and Sex.

Which Article abolished separate communal electoral-roll discrimination? → Article 325.

Which Article establishes Universal Adult Suffrage? → Article 326.

What is the present voting age? → 18 years.

What was the original voting age? → 21 years.

Which Amendment reduced it? → 61st Constitutional Amendment Act, 1988.

Which Article gives Parliament power to make election laws? → Article 327.

Which Article gives State Legislature limited power over its election laws? → Article 328.

Which Article bars court interference during election process? → Article 329.

How is an election ordinarily challenged? → Election Petition after completion.

Which Article deals with President and Vice-President election disputes? → Article 71.

Which Court decides them? → Supreme Court.

What does RPA 1950 mainly deal with? → Electoral rolls, voter registration, allocation of seats and related framework.

What does RPA 1951 mainly deal with? → Conduct of elections, qualifications, disqualifications, corrupt practices, election disputes and party registration.

What is a direct election? → Voters directly elect the representative.

Give examples. → Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies.

What is an indirect election? → Election through an Electoral College or elected body.

Give examples. → President, Vice-President, Rajya Sabha and Legislative Councils.

Which electoral system is used for Lok Sabha and Assemblies? → First-Past-the-Post.

Does a winner require over 50% of votes? → No.

What is required? → Highest number of valid votes.

What system is used in specified indirect elections? → Proportional Representation by Single Transferable Vote.

What does Secret Ballot protect? → Privacy and freedom of electoral choice.

What is a constituency? → Defined territorial area from which a representative is elected.

What is an electoral roll? → Official list of eligible voters.

What age is required for voter registration under the source? → 18 years.

What constitutional body supervises electoral rolls? → Election Commission of India.

What was the original structure of ECI? → Chief Election Commissioner only.

What composition does the attachment record at present? → CEC + two Election Commissioners.

Who appoints CEC? → President.

Who appoints Election Commissioners? → President.

What tenure is stated in the attachment? → Six years or age 65, whichever earlier.

To whom do CEC and ECs resign? → President.

How can CEC be removed? → Same manner and on same grounds as Supreme Court Judge.

How can another Election Commissioner be removed? → On recommendation of CEC.

What types of powers does ECI exercise? → Administrative, Advisory, Quasi-Judicial and Supervisory.

Who recognises National and State political parties? → Election Commission.

Who allots election symbols? → Election Commission.

What is a Reserved Symbol? → Symbol reserved for recognised National or State Party.

What is a Free Symbol? → Symbol available to eligible independents and unrecognised parties under ECI rules.

What is MCC? → Model Code of Conduct.

Who issues and enforces it? → Election Commission.

When does MCC begin? → Immediately after announcement of election schedule.

How long does it continue? → Until completion of election process.

Is MCC a law enacted by Parliament? → No.

What is its central purpose? → Level playing field and fair campaigning.

Can Government machinery be used for partisan campaigning under MCC? → No.

Can public funds be used for electoral advantage? → No.

Can religious places be used for campaigning? → No.

What is delimitation? → Redrawing constituency boundaries.

Who conducts delimitation? → Delimitation Commission.

What is the basic objective? → Fairer population-based representation.

Which groups receive reserved constituencies? → SCs and STs.

What does the source say regarding future seat readjustment? → It is linked to the first Census conducted after 2026, subject to constitutional provisions.

What is the first formal stage after election notification? → Filing of nominations.

Who receives nomination papers? → Returning Officer.

What happens after nominations close? → Scrutiny.

What follows scrutiny? → Withdrawal period.

What follows withdrawal? → Final list and campaign.

What follows campaigning? → Polling.

Who supervises counting? → Returning Officer.

Who is declared elected under FPTP? → Candidate with highest valid votes.

What is an EVM? → Electronic Voting Machine.

What are its main components stated in the attachment? → Ballot Unit, Control Unit and VVPAT where used.

What does VVPAT stand for? → Voter Verifiable Paper Audit Trail.

What is its purpose? → Enable voter to verify recorded vote and provide audit trail.

Can voter take VVPAT slip? → No.

What does EPIC stand for? → Elector Photo Identity Card.

What is its purpose? → Voter identification and prevention of impersonation.

What does NOTA stand for? → None of the Above.

Which case introduced NOTA? → PUCL v. Union of India, 2013.

Does NOTA automatically cancel an election if it receives highest votes under the source framework? → No.

What are important electoral challenges? → Money power, criminalisation, paid news, misuse of Government machinery, misinformation, inducement and hate speech.

Which Article specifies qualifications for Parliament? → Article 84.

Minimum age for Lok Sabha? → 25.

Minimum age for Rajya Sabha? → 30.

Which Article specifies qualifications for State Legislature? → Article 173.

Minimum age for Legislative Assembly? → 25.

Minimum age for Legislative Council? → 30.

Which Article deals with State Legislature disqualification? → Article 191.

Can ECI override an election statute? → No.

Which case established this? → A.C. Jose v. Sivan Pillai, 1984.

Which case upheld the Multi-Member Election Commission? → T.N. Seshan v. Union of India, 1995.
